items.entity: design domain (Fig. 5): size and aspect ratio
items.description: Sec. 3.1 refers only to 'the design domain in Figure 5', meshed with 200×200 bilinear quads; the text gives no side lengths or aspect ratio. Because the load width (0.04) and pad width (0.025) are absolute lengths, the domain size changes their size relative to the domain. A 1×1 square (Δx = 0.005) makes both whole numbers of elements (8 and 5) and fits the reported C ≈ 8.5e-6, but this is never stated.
readings: 1 × 1 square (Δx = 0.005; load = 8 elements, pad = 5 elements)
square of another side, e.g. 2 × 2 (Δx = 0.01) or 0.5 × 0.5 (Δx = 0.0025)
non-square rectangle (e.g. 2 × 1 or 1 × 2) meshed with 200 × 200 non-square elements

items.entity: vertical (u_y) restraints at 'center nodes on each side'
items.description: Sec. 3.1: 'The center nodes on each side of the domain are restricted against vertical displacements.' This can mean only the mid-nodes of the two loaded vertical edges (with u_x = 0 at the centre node, the minimum rigid-body restraint for the self-equilibrated load) or the mid-nodes of all four edges, which adds real u_y supports at the top and bottom mid-points (these only matter for the ω = 1 layout if material reaches them). Only Fig. 5 shows which.
readings: u_y = 0 at mid-nodes of left and right edges only; u_x = 0 at the domain-centre node
u_y = 0 at mid-nodes of all four edges (left, right, top, bottom); u_x = 0 at the domain-centre node

items.entity: two inward horizontal distributed loads (left/right edges, centred on horizontal axis)
items.description: Sec. 3.1: 'L_load = 0.04 with a magnitude of 10^-3 at each load'. It does not say whether 10^-3 is the resultant force, a traction per unit length, or a force per loaded node. With E0 = 1, V = 0.15 and unit thickness, the reported C ≈ 8.5e-6 (ω = 0.5) is just above the straight-bar bound F²/(EV) ≈ 6.7e-6 for F = 1e-3, which favours the resultant reading. The compliance values in Fig. 1(c) (≈1.3–1.4e-3) evidently come from a different, unstated load or setup.
readings: resultant force 1e-3 per load (traction 0.025 per unit length over 0.04)
traction 1e-3 per unit length (resultant 4e-5 per load)
1e-3 on every node of the 0.04 span (9 nodes at Δx = 0.005 → resultant 9e-3)

items.entity: profile and nodal lumping of the 0.04-wide loads
items.description: Sec. 3.1 calls them 'distributed loads' of width 0.04 centred on the horizontal symmetry axis, but gives neither the profile (uniform is implied) nor how it is lumped to nodes. On a 1×1 grid the span covers 9 nodes. The passive pad should keep any effect small and local.
readings: uniform traction with consistent lumping (half weight on the two end nodes of the 9-node span)
equal point forces on all nodes inside the 0.04 span

items.entity: passive solid pads at the two loads
items.description: Sec. 3.1: 'Passive solid regions are located at the loads with a width of 0.025.' Only one dimension is given. It is unclear whether 0.025 runs along the loaded edge (it would then be narrower than the 0.04 load, and a 5-element strip cannot be centred on the mid-line of a 200-element grid with forced symmetry) or is the depth into the domain, and the other dimension is missing. The L-beam pad in Sec. 3.2 ('same width as the load', plus a stated height) suggests load width × 0.025 deep.
readings: 0.04 along the edge (= load width) × 0.025 deep (8 × 5 elements on a 1×1 domain)
≈0.025 × 0.025 square centred on the load (along-edge extent rounded to 4 or 6 elements to keep symmetry)
≈0.025 along the edge × one element deep

items.entity: stiffness interpolation for the ω = 1 (pure-compliance) run
items.description: Sec. 3.1 runs the ω = 1 case twice, once as singlescale SIMP (code [18]) and once as multiscale with the HS upper bound (eq. 8). It only says they give 'similar designs with almost identical performance' (Fig. 8) and does not say which is the reference. The HS-S variant adds a local buckling stress constraint, which a pure minimum-compliance solver cannot represent.
readings: SIMP singlescale (natural choice for a single-material solver)
Hashin–Shtrikman upper-bound interpolation of μ and κ, eq. (8), with E_min = 1e-6 E0, ν = 0.3

items.entity: SIMP penalty exponent and void stiffness (singlescale run)
items.description: Sec. 3.1 says only 'SIMP ... performed using the code from [18]'. No penalty is given for this example (p = 3 is quoted only in the Introduction for Fig. 1), nor whether [18] uses penalty continuation. E_min = 1e-6 E0 is stated only for the HS interpolation.
readings: p = 3 constant, E_min = 1e-6 E0
p = 3 constant, E_min = 1e-9 E0
penalty continuation, e.g. p raised stepwise from 1 to 3

items.entity: density-filter radius when a single design field is used
items.description: Sec. 2.1 sets R_x = 1.5Δx for the density field x and R_s = 4.5Δx for the indicator field s (the field that gets the robust Heaviside projection, Δη = 0.25), 'used throughout'. The SIMP run uses the single-field code [18], and so would a standard single-material solver; the text does not say which radius applies to that one field. The choice sets the robust length scale.
readings: single field, linear-hat filter R = 1.5Δx, robust projection applied to it
single field, R = 4.5Δx, robust projection with η = 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75
two-field scheme ρ = x̃·H(s̃): x filtered with 1.5Δx, s filtered with 4.5Δx and projected

items.entity: lower bound x_min of the infill density field
items.description: Eq. (19) imposes x_min ≤ x_j ≤ 1, but Sec. 3.1 gives no x_min. The only value in the paper, 0.27, belongs to the L-beam (Sec. 3.2) and is justified by de-homogenization resolution. It matters for the HS/two-field run, not for single-field SIMP.
readings: x_min = 0 (or ~1e-3)
x_min = 0.27 (as in Sec. 3.2)
x_min = 0.1 (lowest density characterised by the Bloch–Floquet analysis)

items.entity: initial design of the ω = 1 runs
items.description: Sec. 3.1 says the ω = 1 runs come first (later ω values restart from the previous designs) but not where they start. Sec. 3.2 mentions only 'uniform initial guesses' with no values. With two fields (x, s), a start at volume 0.15 can be split in several ways.
readings: uniform ρ = 0.15 (single field)
uniform x = 1, s = 0.15
uniform x = 0.15, s = 1
uniform x = s = √0.15 ≈ 0.39

items.description: Sec. 3: 'β is initialized as β = 2. After the first 125 iterations β is doubled every 75 iterations until β_max = 256 is reached.' The first doubling could be at iteration 125 or at iteration 200, which shifts the end of continuation by 75 iterations.
readings: doublings at iterations 125, 200, …, 575 (β = 256 from iteration 575)
doublings at iterations 200, 275, …, 650 (β = 256 from iteration 650)

items.description: No maximum iteration count or convergence tolerance is given anywhere (Secs. 2–3), so it is unknown how long the run continues at β_max = 256 before the final design is taken.
readings: stop as soon as β = 256 is reached
fixed number of further iterations at β = 256 (e.g. 75–200)
stop on a design-change tolerance at β_max (e.g. max|Δx| < 1e-3 or 1e-2)

items.entity: update of the dilated-design volume bound V_d*
items.description: Sec. 2: V_d* 'is continuously updated to ensure that the target volume V_b* is enforced on the blue print design' (V_b* = 0.15, Sec. 3.1). Neither the update rule nor its frequency is given. A solver without a robust formulation would apply 0.15 directly to the physical design.
readings: every iteration: V_d* = 0.15·V(ρ^d)/V(ρ^b)
same rescaling every N (e.g. 20) iterations
volume constraint 0.15 applied directly to the blueprint/physical design

items.description: Only MMA [40] is named (Sec. 2.2.3). Move limits, asymptote parameters and how the min–max over the eroded/blueprint/dilated designs is posed are not given. The SIMP run's optimizer comes from code [18] and is not described.
readings: default Svanberg MMA parameters, bound formulation for the max over designs
MMA with move limit 0.1–0.2
optimality-criteria (OC) update as in standard compliance codes

items.description: No element thickness is given. Plane stress is implied by κ0 = E0/(2(1−ν0)), and the thickness only scales the compliance value.
readings: unit thickness t = 1
other thickness t (C ∝ 1/t)
